articles.title: President's Message September 2018
articles.summary: The September 2018 President's Message from Swami Nigam welcomes members, shares his personal journey with SJAA, and outlines key initiatives focused on automating operations and increasing member participation. It details significant personnel transitions, including the departures of long-serving Vice President Bill O'Neil and School Star Party lead Jim Van Nuland, the stepping down of content editor Sandy Mohan, and the passing of Phil Chambers. The message also introduces new volunteers taking on various leadership roles within the club.

articles.title: SJAA's School Star Party Needs Your Help!
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is seeking volunteers for its School Star Party (SSP) program after long-time leader Jim Van Nuland retired. New leaders Cat Cvengros and Peter Mu are now at the helm, aiming to continue the program's mission of bringing astronomy education to hundreds of young people and families. The article outlines specific volunteer roles, including SSP Liaisons, Scouts, and Astronomers, encouraging interested individuals to contribute to this impactful community outreach initiative.

articles.title: New Solar Loaner Telescope and Kit Details
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) has introduced a new Lunt 50 H-α solar telescope to its Advanced Loaner Program, available to members as of August. This article details the comprehensive kit, which includes a double-stacking etalon filter, explaining the importance of hydrogen-alpha viewing for observing prominences and filaments, especially during solar minimum. It also provides technical insights into etalon filters and outlines the borrowing procedures and requirements for qualified SJAA members.

articles.title: Bill O'Neil Resignation Letter
articles.summary: Bill O'Neil announces his resignation from the SJAA Board of Directors and his role as Vice President, effective August 12, 2018, as he and his wife are moving to Seattle, Washington. He reflects on his extensive contributions to the SJAA, including leading the Starry Nights and Solar Programs, serving as VP, and his involvement in public outreach and the Houge Park contract. O'Neil expresses confidence in the SJAA's leadership and plans to maintain his membership.

articles.title: Editor's note
articles.summary: Sandy Mohan, the outgoing Editor of Ephemeris, reflects on her five years in the role and her long-standing involvement with the SJAA, which began in 2000 through her sons' rekindled interest in astronomy. She recounts her personal journey, highlights the club's resources and the newsletter's evolution, and expresses gratitude while wishing the new editor success.

articles.title: Cambrian Fest 2018
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) participated for the ninth consecutive year in San Jose's 'Celebrate Cambrian' community fair on August 26, 2018. Volunteers hosted a booth featuring multiple solar telescopes, including a Lunt H-alpha scope and a camera-equipped rig displaying live solar views, showcasing a prominence and a filament on the sun. The event successfully engaged the public and students, with activities like UV-sensitive bead bracelets, fostering community outreach and interest in astronomy.

articles.title: Traveling to the Sun: Why Won't Parker Solar Probe Melt?
articles.summary: NASA's Parker Solar Probe launched to travel closer to the Sun's corona than any previous mission, aiming to provide unprecedented observations of solar phenomena. Despite encountering temperatures exceeding a million degrees Fahrenheit, the probe is designed not to melt thanks to its custom Thermal Protection System (TPS) heat shield, autonomous navigation, and a specialized water-based cooling system. The design leverages the distinction between temperature and heat, recognizing that the low density of the corona limits actual heat transfer to the spacecraft.

articles.title: Local Author and Astronomer Honored with an Asteroid Named for Him
articles.summary: Bob Garfinkle, a longtime SJAA member, author, and astronomer, has been honored with an asteroid officially named "(31862) Garfinkle" by the International Astronomical Union (IAU). The asteroid, located in the main belt, is approximately 6 km in diameter. Garfinkle is also a Fellow of the Royal Astronomical Society, a best-selling author of astronomy books, and holds various other prestigious positions in astronomical and writing organizations.

articles.title: Hubble's Messier Telescope
articles.summary: This article details the life and work of Charles Messier, a French astronomer known for compiling the "Catalog of Nebulae and Star Clusters" to help comet hunters distinguish comets from other deep-sky objects. It highlights the Messier catalog's enduring popularity among amateur astronomers due to the visibility of its 110 objects and describes how the Hubble Space Telescope has contributed significantly to imaging 96 of these objects, offering detailed views and scientific insights through multi-wavelength observations.

articles.title: Kid Spot
articles.summary: This article features a "Kid Spot" section offering astronomy-themed jokes and a quiz, alongside a report on the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). SJAA hosted a movie screening for "Saving The Dark," a film by Sriram Murali dedicated to raising awareness about light pollution and its impact on observing the night sky and the environment. The association sponsored the movie with $1000 and renewed its membership with the International Dark Sky Association (IDA) with a $100 donation, committing to further publicize the film.

articles.title: From the Board of Directors
articles.summary: This report from the SJAA Board of Directors details key announcements and discussions from June and July 2018. Significant personnel changes include Bill O'Neil's resignation as Director and VP due to relocation, and Ken Miura's appointment to a vacant board seat. The report also covers updates on the City of San Jose contract, the acquisition of a new solar telescope for the loaner program, and initiatives such as an apprentice program, establishing an Instagram presence, and a sponsorship for the 'Saving the Dark' movie.

articles.title: SJAA Library
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) provides a comprehensive suite of resources and programs for its members and the community, catering to all ages and skill levels. Offerings include a library, free telescope repair, solar observing sessions, beginner-friendly programs like Quick STARt and Intro to the Night Sky, an equipment loaner program, and dedicated groups and workshops for astrophotography. SJAA also hosts public and school star parties, fostering engagement and education in astronomy.
